rationale.complete: Round 1 done on 32 non-holdout goal periods plus NE42: dated predictions in the card and every period folder, synthetic validation on three real skeletons (240 runs) with a synthetic-only amendment before real data, per-period verdicts, scorecard, 8 robustness variants, a labelled post-hoc sensitivity (A2). Confirmatory script for #28/#22/#14 frozen and dry-run (reproduces round 1), not run. Not done: per-message coupling, agenda-setting event study, style control, second embedding model, #51. Round 1b (2026-10-04): re-run on context-ledger exposure, gte and style-residualized embeddings, statement dedupe, an H57 read-vs-in-flight placebo, and three leader natives (#26 real term, #35 lead designers, #44 window).
rationale.faithfulness: The leader claim failed by its own pre-registered rules: humans as a known source rank above the median agent in only 4/16 periods, the elected #26 leader ranks 7/10 after the vote, the #44 operator 5/7. A source stands out in 2/18 periods, and NE42 shows no switch-on. What holds is narrower: transfer beats the cross-day shift null in 18/32 periods (15/32 within-day too), depends on exposure (7/8 multi-room weeks), and the outflow ranking replicates across halves (23/26). The level is sensitive to field removal, and the top-source identity is not robust. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E0 F1 G1 H1 I0. Round 1b: replicates on ledger exposure; existence robust across embedding models but the top source's identity is not (17/32); at matched short lag read > in-flight in 17/17 but in-flight carries about a third; all leader natives fail as predicted. Axes unchanged.
rationale.usefulness: A computable diagnostic from chat logs: total content transfer T, a reproducible outflow ranking, and a 'does any source stand out' test, with measured synthetic accuracy and a known confound (fast responders). The actionable lesson is negative but relevant for steering: installed or elected leaders do not become content sources, and an installed fine-tuned leader was the most-influenced agent in its room. It does not tell an operator where to intervene.

one_line: Content transfer between agents is real (17-23/32 periods, read > in-flight at matched lag 17/17) but model-dependent in who leads, and elected, designated, installed and operator leaders are not content sources

v2.claim: Exposure-gated content transfer is real (17/32 periods; read beats unread at 60 s in 17/17), but about a third of it is convergence; formal leaders are not content sources (3/3 natives); which agent leads depends on the embedding model

ladder.factor: partly robust (gte 23/32, style 18/32; top source model-dependent)
rival beaten (read vs in-flight at matched lag)
